tasks.title: Write the product specification (no technical content)
tasks.description: Interview the user on what the desktop application should do and how it should work from their point of view, then write it up in the OpenSpec convention under openspec/ in this goal directory: a project context document plus one spec per capability, each with SHALL requirements illustrated by WHEN/THEN scenarios.
tasks.notes: Seven capabilities written: application-shell, item-catalog, recipe-library, material-calculation, hangar, production-plans, data-storage, plus openspec/project.md and openspec/README.md. README.md carries a what-changed-vs-the-web-version table and a list of nine decisions that were derived from the interview rather than stated outright, for the user to check.

tasks.title: Review and sign off the specification
tasks.description: User reads openspec/ end to end and either confirms it or corrects it. Particular attention to the nine derived decisions listed at the bottom of openspec/README.md - recipe-vs-blueprint wording, whether a hangar reset should also clear steps already marked done, mandatory distinct T2 variant labels, refusing to delete a recipe an open plan targets, Acquire entries not being tickable, a fixed rather than chosen data folder, pastes storing nothing before recipes exist, cycle detection on save, and the single-window layout being Claude's choice. Nothing downstream should start until this is settled.
tasks.notes: Signed off 2026-10-04 after a review pass. Claude fixed the clear-cut contradictions itself, then the user decided the open points one by one. Outcomes: started steps are fixed in place, recording their figures, and their output counts as on its way; done steps go to a collapsed section; in a reserved plan, finished output goes to the pile only up to what the plan needs, with batch surplus going to general stock; a reserved plan draws only on its pile, and editing or deleting a recipe it uses or changing its variant choice releases the reservation after a warning; reserving stays all-or-nothing, and inputs leave the pile when a step starts; a hangar reset clears started and done steps of incomplete plans but leaves completed plans alone; a fourth sidebar section, Items; the target product is never netted against stock, so a plan completes only when its final step is done; no buy-instead-of-build; plan size is entered in runs and fixed at creation; one recipe type per product, and adding a second T2 variant asks for both labels in place; stock of an item no recipe uses any more stays and is flagged; an item holding stock cannot be deleted; no manual add-item action, since a typed paste line does the job; fractional quantities permanently out of scope; data records the app version that wrote it; malformed or newer-version data shows an error and the app does not start against it; only one copy runs at a time; hand edits only while the app is closed.

tasks.title: Choose the tech stack
tasks.description: Decide how the desktop application is built and packaged for Windows, judged against the signed-off specification. Weigh reuse of the existing Angular UI work against a fresh start, and factor in the data-storage requirements (readable files, automatic migration on upgrade) and the user's Docker-only development setup. Record the choice and the reasoning as a key decision on this goal.
tasks.notes: User delegated the choice to Claude. Chosen: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + Vite; domain logic in TypeScript behind a storage interface, with a thin Rust file layer; native Windows toolchain, not Docker. Full reasoning is in goal.json key_decisions.

tasks.title: Design the data file format and folder layout
tasks.description: Settle the concrete shape of what data-storage/spec.md describes in behavioural terms: which files exist, what format each uses (the user ruled out anything not human-readable and suggested CSV, XML or YAML), how items, categories, recipes, hangar stock and plans are laid out across them, and how a file identifies which application version wrote it so migration and the refuse-to-open-newer-data rule can work.
tasks.notes: Design written to design/data-files.md and decisions recorded in goal.json (2026-10-04). Spec updated: production-plans gained 'Completed plans are removed after a week' and 'Plans and steps show when things happened'. User reviewed and accepted the design, including Claude's calls on removal-only-at-start, showing the removal date, the 'EVE' spelling, missing-file-is-an-error, local-time-with-offset timestamps, and dangling references in stored steps being allowed.

tasks.title: Design the upgrade and migration mechanism
tasks.description: Work out how a newly installed build detects an older data layout, converts it, keeps the pre-conversion copy, and reports what it did - and how it refuses to touch data written by a newer build. This is the concrete answer to the user's 'a way to patch it without losing the data' requirement.
tasks.notes: Design in design/upgrades.md, decision recorded in goal.json. User decided: refuse by format version rather than app version (data-storage spec revised: new scenarios for going back to an older build, with or without a format change), and backups inside the data folder. data-files.md cross-references it, and its commit protocol gained file deletion for conversions.

tasks.title: Break the implementation into tasks
tasks.description: Once stack, file format and migration approach are decided, decompose the implementation capability by capability and add the resulting tasks to this file. Suggested order follows the dependency chain: item catalog, then recipe library, then the calculation engine, then the hangar, then production plans, with the application shell growing alongside them.
tasks.notes: Broken down into tasks 8-33, listed in working order. Every implementation task carries a 'Testing:' section: automated tests (Vitest, cargo test) wherever possible, and explicit manual checks for the user where something cannot be tested that way. The application-shell spec lost 'reopen the plan last open' during this review: the app starts on the list of incomplete plans and remembers no UI state between runs.

tasks.title: Decide the fate of the existing Angular/PHP/Docker application
tasks.description: Once the desktop app covers the specification, decide whether the frontend/, backend/, docker-compose.yml and scripts/ parts of the repository are removed, archived on a branch, or kept running alongside. (5_make_production_ready, which was about hardening the container setup, was already closed as superseded on 2026-10-04.)
tasks.notes: Decided 2026-10-04: leave the old app exactly as it is in frontend/ and backend/ for now. The new app gets its own top-level directory, desktop_app/, in this repository. Revisit only if the user raises it.

tasks.title: Install the Windows development toolchain
tasks.description:
Install Node LTS, Rust (rustup, stable, MSVC target) and the Visual Studio Build Tools with the 'Desktop development with C++' workload on the Windows host. WebView2 ships with Windows 11. The user runs the installers; Claude gives the exact steps.

Testing: manual by the user, then verified by Claude: `node -v`, `npm -v`, `rustc -V` and `cargo -V` all answer from a fresh terminal.
tasks.notes: Installed via winget: Visual Studio Build Tools 2022 17.14 (VCTools workload, MSVC x64 verified with vswhere), rustup 1.29.1 -> rustc/cargo 1.99.0 on stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, Node 24.19.0 LTS / npm 11.17.0. WebView2 154 was already present. winget run through Claude Code's `!` prefix cannot answer prompts: add `--source winget --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements`, otherwise it fails with 0x8a150042 on the msstore terms prompt.

tasks.title: Scaffold the Tauri app in desktop_app/
tasks.description:
Create the Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + Vite project in desktop_app/ at the repository root, beside the old frontend/ and backend/. Add Vitest, ESLint and the Tauri single-instance plugin, which brings the open window to the front on a second launch. Folder layout separates the domain core (pure TypeScript, no UI or I/O), the storage interface and its adapters, and the UI. One source of truth for the app version. npm scripts: dev (desktop window), dev:browser (plain browser using the browser storage adapter), test, lint, build. Add desktop_app/node_modules and desktop_app/src-tauri/target to .gitignore.

Testing: automated - a trivial Vitest test and a cargo test run green, and lint passes. Manual (user) - `npm run dev` opens a window; starting it a second time brings the first window to the front instead of opening another.
tasks.notes: Scaffolded with create-tauri-app (react-ts), then reworked: identifier de.senjiu.eve-industry-calculator (confirmed by the user; must not change after the first real release), productName 'EVE Industry Calculator', NSIS bundle target. Version lives only in package.json (tauri.conf.json uses "version": "../package.json", the UI gets it via a Vite define). Layout src/core, src/storage, src/ui; ESLint no-restricted-imports keeps core free of UI/storage/React/Tauri and storage free of UI. Scripts: dev, dev:browser, test (vitest + cargo test), lint (tsc -b + eslint + clippy -D warnings), build, build:web. Automated: 4 Vitest + 1 cargo test green, lint clean. Manual (user): window opens, second launch exits at once and brings the existing window to the front. Note: the dev binary is target/debug/eve_industry_calculator.exe (crate name); mainBinaryName only applies to the bundle. Root .gitignore unchanged - the nested .gitignore files already exclude node_modules, target and gen/schemas.

tasks.title: Data model, serialisation and load-time validation
tasks.description:
Implement design/data-files.md in the domain core: TypeScript types for manifest/items/recipes/hangar/plans. A serialiser that pretty-prints with two-space indentation, fixed key order, alphabetical maps, omitted optional fields, LF endings and a trailing newline. A JSON reader that rejects repeated keys and reports line numbers. Full validation of every rule listed under 'Validation on load', producing file + line (or data path) + expected-vs-found errors.

Testing: automated - round trip (parse then serialise is byte-identical); every validation rule has a failing-input test asserting the file, line and message; the repeated-key test; CRLF input accepted.
tasks.notes: Code in desktop_app/src/core/data/: jsonParse (own strict parser with lines, repeated-key detection, BOM + CRLF accepted), jsonWrite (writes from explicit entry lists, since JS objects reorder integer-like keys), model, serialize, decode (per-file structure/types, collects all errors in a file, records path -> line), validate (cross-file rules incl. cycle detection), load (orchestrates; cross-file checks skipped while any file is broken). Name-keyed maps are Map, not objects. Fixture data folder in src/core/data/fixtures/format-1/ (illustrative quantities, not real EVE recipes) - task 12 reuses it. User decisions this session: unknown keys are malformed; a product's only recipe MAY carry a variant label; report all errors where cheap, but a syntax error stops that file and cross-file checks only run once every file is sound. Claude's calls: names (items, categories, labels) with leading/trailing spaces or empty are malformed; empty variant label is malformed (omit instead); quantities must be plain integer literals (no 1.0 / 1e3) within the exact integer range; timestamps must have an explicit offset (no Z); per-state step rules (started needs started+deducted and may not have done/addedTo*; done needs done+addedToReserved+addedToGeneral); a completed plan with 'reserved' is malformed; an empty reserved pile {} is valid and still means reserved; a completed plan's target item is NOT checked (otherwise deleting the recipe and then the item after completion would produce data the app refuses to load - contradicts data-files.md's 'plan targets name an existing item' for completed plans). 112 Vitest tests green, lint clean.

tasks.title: Storage layer: file commands, atomic commit, browser adapter
tasks.description:
Thin Rust commands: read file, write and flush file, rename, delete, list, copy, resolve Documents via the Windows known-folder API, and open a folder in Explorer, with retry and backoff on rename for OneDrive locks. In TypeScript, behind the storage interface: the commit protocol from data-files.md (tmp files, commit.json as the commit point, renames, replace + delete lists) and start-up recovery (roll forward / discard). A browser storage adapter for dev:browser.

Testing: automated - the commit protocol and recovery run against an in-memory fake file system, simulating a crash after every individual operation and asserting the folder always ends up wholly before or wholly after; cargo tests for the Rust commands against a temp directory. Manual (user) - none expected.
tasks.notes: Rust (src-tauri/src/files.rs + commands in lib.rs): read_text, write_text (sync_all), rename (MoveFileExW REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH, retry 25..800 ms on os errors 5/32/33), remove (missing = ok), list (missing folder = empty), copy (+flush; needs write access on Windows), create_dir, exists, open_folder (opener plugin), data_folder. All take paths relative to the data folder; '..', absolute paths, empty segments etc. are refused. Data folder resolved once in setup via app.path().document_dir() (known-folder API). USER DECISION: debug builds use 'Documents\EVE Industry Calculator (dev)', release builds the real folder. TS (src/storage/): FileSystem + DataFolder interfaces, tauriDataFolder, MemoryFileSystem (fake with crashAfter(n), torn writes, failOn), BrowserFileSystem (MemoryFileSystem persisted to localStorage), commit.ts (commit + recover; CommitError.committed says whether the change took effect; a failure after the commit point retries via recover once). Tests: 16 cargo (incl. a real locked-file retry), 24 Vitest for storage incl. crash after every op of a commit, crash at every op of recovery after each of those, torn write. Mutation check: moving a rename before the commit point makes 5 tests fail. The Tauri adapter itself is only exercised end-to-end once task 12 uses it.

tasks.title: Start-up sequence and data conversion framework
tasks.description:
Implement design/upgrades.md: create the folder on first start; read the manifest; start, convert or refuse by formatVersion; a conversion-step chain (empty for format 1) run in memory and validated; backup to backups\format A to B - <date time>\; commit; the one-off conversion message; the refuse-newer and malformed-data error screens, with 'open data folder' and 'try again'. Add the format-1 fixture data folder and the schema-snapshot guard test.

Testing: automated - every start-up test listed in upgrades.md, using a test-only fake conversion step to exercise the convert path; malformed data leaves files byte-identical. Manual (user) - hand-break a file while the app is closed and check that the error names the right file and line, then fix it and press try again.
tasks.notes: Automated: 177 Vitest + 16 cargo tests, lint clean. Manual (user, 2026-10-04): broke items.json both as invalid JSON and as valid JSON with a misspelt key; both gave good messages, and Try again started normally once fixed. core/data/format.ts: CURRENT_FORMAT = 1, CONVERSION_STEPS = [], convertData (chain in memory, then validated by serialising to text and running loadData; files left over that the new format lacks are an error, not silently deleted), emptyData. decode.ts now exports FIELDS/ENUMS (complete since unknown keys are rejected); fixtures/format-1.schema.json snapshots them and format.test.ts fails with instructions when the shape changes without a format bump (mutation-checked). app/startup.ts: recover -> create folder on first start -> read only formatVersion/writtenBy leniently (so a newer format with a changed manifest is still recognised as newer) -> start / refuse / convert (backup to backups/format A to B - YYYY-MM-DD HH-mm with ' (2)' suffix, then one commit incl. deletes). Tests use a made-up 'format 1' (fixtures/olderFormat.ts, stock.json -> hangar.json) with currentFormat injected as 2, incl. a crash after every operation of a conversion. app/oneAtATime.ts serialises start-up runs (React StrictMode runs effects twice in dev); all later writes must go through it too. UI: ui/Startup.tsx with error screens (malformed / newer / conversionFailed / failed), open-folder + try-again, one-off conversion notice in App. Seven-day plan removal (step 5 of the sequence) is left to task 28. Verified end to end: npm run dev created Documents\EVE Industry Calculator (dev) with the five files and no leftovers.

tasks.title: Application shell
tasks.description:
One window: a sidebar with Plans / Recipes / Hangar / Items, and a main panel that keeps each section's state while switching within a session (nothing is remembered across restarts). The start-up landing pages from application-shell/spec.md (list of incomplete plans / create-a-plan / create-your-first-recipe). A data-folder panel with the full path, an open-folder button and the 'edit files only while the app is closed' note. Shared building blocks: a confirmation dialog that states the consequences, failures explained in place without losing input, and the app-state pattern where each action computes the new data in memory, commits it in one atomic write, and only then updates the screen.

Testing: automated - component tests for landing-page selection and confirmation dialogs; an action that fails to commit leaves the in-memory state unchanged. Manual (user) - look and feel of the layout, and section switching keeping its place.
tasks.notes: Manual check by the user 2026-10-04: window, landing page and section switching fine. User asked for sidebar entries 100% taller (y only) and text 50% bigger: now min-height 54px, font-size 1.5em, sidebar widened 140 -> 180px so labels and counts fit (Claude's call). User may want more colour later; main panels to be judged once they have real content. app/store.ts: DataStore - apply(change) runs in the shared write queue, computes new data in memory (or refuse(reason)), serialises all files, commits only those that differ plus manifest.json with writtenBy = this build, re-validates the texts with loadData before writing (never writes data the next start would refuse), and only then updates current data and notifies subscribers. Failed commit -> state unchanged, status failed; CommitError.committed -> adopted with a warning. app/oneAtATime.ts gained createQueue(); main.tsx shares one queue between start-up and the store. ui/context.ts: StoreContext, useAppData (useSyncExternalStore), useAction (failure/warning kept for showing in place), NavigationContext/useGoTo, ConfirmContext/useConfirm. ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx (alertdialog, consequences list, action-named confirm button, Cancel focused, Escape cancels). ui/Failure.tsx. ui/Shell.tsx: 140px dark sidebar with counts (Plans = open plans, Recipes, Hangar, Items) plus Data folder and version at the foot; all sections stay mounted and are hidden, so switching keeps their state. Plans landing per spec: open plans table / recipes table with no open plans (user's preference matched this: 'just the list of recipes') / explanation + Create the first recipe button. Recipes, Hangar and Items show simple read-only tables as placeholders until their tasks; Items has a search box. User gave no layout preferences up front: Claude builds, user requests changes. 200 Vitest tests green, lint clean.

tasks.title: Recipe validation rules
tasks.description:
Domain-core validation for saving a recipe: at least one input; positive whole quantities; no self-consumption; duplicate inputs detected so they can be offered for combining; one recipe per product except T2 Manufacturing; distinct non-empty variant labels when there are several; one recipe type per product; cycle detection that returns the chain (A to B to C to A).

Testing: automated - one test per recipe-library validation scenario, plus cycle cases of length 2, 3 and through a T2 variant.
tasks.notes: core/recipes/saveRecipe.ts: saveRecipe(data, draft, {original?, existingLabel?}) -> AppData | Refusal<RecipeProblem[]>, every problem tied to a form field (product/type/variant/existingLabel/output/inputs/{rows}). Rules: product and inputs must be catalog items; output and quantities whole >= 1; at least one input; duplicate rows reported together with their combined total (combineDuplicateInputs merges into the first row); no self-consumption; mixed types (names existing recipe + type); only T2 may have several (names existing); T2 siblings need distinct labels ignoring case; existing unlabelled T2 sibling -> existingNeedsLabel, then saved together with existingLabel; changing the product of a recipe an incomplete plan targets is refused (targetedByPlans) when no other recipe for the old product remains; cycles via validate.findCycles over the library after the save, rotated to start at the input that closes the loop (A -> B -> C -> A for C made from A) and reported on that row; cycle check only runs once the record is otherwise sound. Label changes (edit, or labelling the existing recipe) move plan targets and variantChoices along. NOT done here, left to task 30: explicit variantChoices for plans that implicitly used a previously sole unlabelled recipe as an intermediate (needs the calculation engine). Tests assert every successful save reloads via loadData. 34 tests; 279 Vitest total, lint clean.

tasks.title: Calculation engine
tasks.description:
The material-calculation spec as pure domain code. Inputs: recipes, a target recipe and run count, available material, variant choices, and the plan's started and done steps. Covers recursive expansion to base materials with consolidated totals; whole runs; leftover shared within one calculation; netting against available material at every tier, never against the target product; started steps' output counted as already on its way; dependency build order with a stable order within a tier; and a 'variant choice needed' result instead of a guess or a failure. Output: Acquire entries, Build entries and base material totals, including fully covered materials.

Testing: automated - every material-calculation scenario as a test, the 'reserving across tiers' X/y/z example from production-plans, deep multi-tier fixtures modelled on real T2/PI/reaction chains, and stability of the build order across repeated runs.
tasks.notes: core/calculation/calculate.ts: calculate({recipes, target, runs, available, variantChoices, steps}) -> {acquire, builds, baseMaterials, fromAvailable, choicesNeeded} or {ok:false, reason:'targetMissing'}. Items are processed consumers-first (reverse DFS post-order over the chosen recipes), so each item's total demand is known before its runs are computed: shared batches, leftover < one run's output, and netting at every tier fall out. Per item: available covers first (recorded in fromAvailable - exactly what a reservation moves, intermediates included), then output of started steps on its way, then whole runs. The target is never netted; only runs of started/done target steps reduce it. Done intermediate steps count only via the stock they produced. Started steps appear as entries with their recorded figures; their surplus is leftover on the last one started for that product; a started step the tree no longer needs sits just before the target. Variants: choice used if valid; sole recipe used without asking; otherwise (several, or an invalid remembered choice) a ChoiceNeeded entry with labels, invalidChoice and stillNeeded, and nothing below it is expanded - the rest still calculates. Build order: by tier (0 = base, else 1 + highest input tier; target last), then name, then started before new - stable regardless of recipe/input order. 26 tests incl. every material-calculation scenario, the X/y/z reservation example, a deep T2/PI/reaction fixture (made-up quantities), order stability; mutation-checked (4 mutations, all caught). 349 Vitest, lint clean. Trace/explanation is task 21.

tasks.title: Calculation explanation
tasks.description:
Extend the engine so every step and material carries its trace: the total demand, which parts of the tree it came from, how much was covered by available material, the run count it rounds up to, and the leftover. This feeds the 'why is this number what it is' view in the plan.

Testing: automated - the trace for the 'tracing a quantity' scenario and for a shared-batch case adds up exactly to the reported figures.
tasks.notes: calculate() result gained trace: Map<item, ItemTrace> for every item reached with demand, target included. ItemTrace: how (build/acquire/choice/target), demandFrom (each consuming product and its quantity, sorted by name - the immediate parents; the user drills up through them), totalDemand, fromAvailable, onItsWay (started steps), remaining, and for builds/target outputPerRun, runs, produced, leftover. Invariants tested on a deep tree with stock: fromAvailable + onItsWay + remaining = totalDemand; demandFrom sums to totalDemand; produced = runs x outputPerRun = remaining + leftover; matches the build entry. Also: a base material with output on its way (only possible for a started step whose recipe was deleted) now reports toAcquire = remaining. The UI for it is part of task 25. 30 engine tests.

tasks.title: Hangar paste reader
tasks.description:
Parse pasted inventory/assets text: the first token made only of digits, dots and commas is the quantity, the text before it is the name, the rest is ignored. Keep only items some recipe references, as input or product. Produce the summary of what was added (with quantities), ignored (not used by any recipe) and skipped (no quantity). Pasting adds to existing stock.

Testing: automated - every hangar paste scenario, including tab-separated inventory lines, assets lines with trailing columns, names containing digits (F77 Compact Co-Processor), thousands separators, and pasting twice. Manual (user) - paste real text copied from the game's inventory and assets windows, since its exact format can only be checked against the game.
tasks.notes: Manual check by the user 2026-10-05: real text copied from the in-game hangar (inventory) window pasted correctly, and a typed line works. Real assets-window text with industry items also pasted correctly. core/hangar/paste.ts: readPasteLines (tokens split on tab and plain space only; quantity = first token matching digits plus . , no-break space U+00A0 and narrow no-break space U+202F - the last two are Claude's addition beyond the spec, for game locales using them as thousands separators; name = text before it, trimmed; blank lines ignored; no quantity, empty name or 0 -> skipped) and pasteStock (names matched ignoring case, stored as the catalog spells them; kept only if some recipe uses the item as input or product; otherwise ignored with reason notAnItem / notUsedByRecipe; lines naming the same item summed; adds to general stock, never replaces). 18 tests incl. inventory and assets formats, F77 Compact Co-Processor, punctuation-led names, separators, pasting twice.

tasks.title: Step transitions
tasks.description:
Start (deduct inputs from the reserved pile or general stock, record the snapshot and the start time, warn on shortfall listing items and amounts, clamp at zero, record the shortfall). Done (add output: all to general stock if unreserved; up to the plan's need into the pile and the batch surplus to general stock if reserved). Done without starting (offer to deduct and record output in one action, or record output only). Revert done to started and started to not started, returning exactly what was moved, clamping at zero and recording what could not be removed. Every transition is a single atomic commit.

Testing: automated - every step scenario in production-plans (starting a reaction, a reserved start, starting short, declining the warning, batch surplus, completing without starting, all revert cases, a recipe edited while a step is started).
tasks.notes: Built 2026-10-06, awaiting the user's manual check (work through a real plan). User decision 2026-10-06: undoing a step that was marked done WITHOUT being started goes straight back to not started (step removed, deducted inputs returned, output removed; anything not removable is only warned about, since the step is gone) - data-files.md only covered done -> started. core/plans/steps.ts: EntryRef (product/variant/runs as shown; acting refuses entryChanged if the recalculated checklist no longer has it), StepRef (index guarded by product+state), startShortfall (preview, changes nothing), startStep (deducts from pile if reserved else general, clamps, records deducted/short/started and the recipe figures), completeStep (reserved: output into the pile up to trace.onItsWay of the product - i.e. what the plan still needs beyond its pile - rest to general; target output all to pile; unreserved: all general), completeDirectly (virtual start with or without deducting, complete, then drop the start time), revertShortfall (preview of output that can no longer be removed), revertStep (done -> started: remove addedToReserved from the pile if still reserved else general, addedToGeneral from general, clamp, notRemoved recorded; started -> not started: deducted back to pile if takenFrom reserved and still reserved, else general; step removed). Completing a plan (part of task 28) is in complete(): when the done target runs reach plan.runs with no target step still started, completed = now and the whole pile goes to general stock. Steps of a completed plan refuse with planCompleted. UI: ConfirmDialog gained a second option (useChoose / ChoiceRequest.alternativeLabel); ui/sections/stepActions.ts useStepActions(at); checklist rows: not started -> Start / Done, started -> Done / Undo start, plus Details; started rows show shortfall and notRemoved; done section rows have Undo done (or Undo for directly-done steps), hidden on completed plans. Start short -> Start anyway dialog listing the shortfall; Done without start -> Deduct inputs and add output / Add output only; Undo of spent output -> Undo anyway. 23 domain tests (each outcome also serialised and loaded again) + 6 component tests. 463 Vitest, lint + clippy clean. User checked 2026-10-06: everything works.

tasks.title: Finishing plans and seven-day removal
tasks.description:
A plan completes exactly when its final build step is marked done: the completion time is recorded and the whole pile, finished product included, goes to general stock. Holding the target product in stock never completes a plan. On every start, plans completed more than seven days ago are removed in one commit, with the hangar untouched; completed plans show their removal date.

Testing: automated - the finishing-a-plan scenarios; removal at 6 days 23 hours (kept) vs 7 days 1 hour (removed) using an injected clock; removal does not happen mid-session.
tasks.notes: Partly done with task 26 (2026-10-06): completion on marking the last target step done, completion time, pile (product included) back to general stock, completed plans read-only, removal date shown in the list and plan view (removalDate in core/plans/plans.ts). Still open: removal of plans completed more than seven days ago on every start (one commit, hangar untouched, injected clock), and its tests. Rest done 2026-10-06: core/plans/retention.ts removeExpiredPlans(data, now: Date) - more than 7 x 24 h between instants (Date parses the stored offset); returns the same object when nothing expires. app/startup.ts runs it after every ready start (equal format or after a conversion) and, only if something was removed, commits plans.json + manifest.json (writtenBy brought up to date) before anything is shown. tasks.title: Recipe changes that affect plans
tasks.description:
Saving an edited recipe used by incomplete plans names them and asks for confirmation; reserved ones are named as being released. Deleting a recipe targeted by an incomplete plan is refused, naming the plans. Deleting a recipe used as an intermediate states the consequence (becomes a base material, or another variant must be chosen) and releases reservations. Adding a second T2 variant writes explicit variant choices into the plans that were implicitly using the first one, in the same commit.

Testing: automated - every 'changing a recipe that plans depend on' scenario, plus 'a second variant is added later' and 'a remembered choice becomes invalid' from material-calculation.
tasks.notes: Built 2026-10-12. User chose: a plan counts as affected only when its outstanding work changes (acquire, build steps/runs/inputs ignoring order and labels, choices needed, what it draws from available) - not merely when the recipe is somewhere in its tree. core/recipes/planImpact.ts: plansChangedBy(before, after) recalculates each incomplete plan both ways; releaseChanged releases affected reserved plans; planReaches walks the recipe tree structurally (stock-independent). saveRecipe and deleteRecipe now release affected reservations in the same commit; saveRecipe writes the existing recipe's label as an explicit variant choice into incomplete plans that reached the product through its only recipe when a second variant is added (also when the existing one is labelled in the same save; also when stock currently covers it). Deleting a chosen variant keeps the stale choice so the plan asks again. UI: recipe form previews the save - an edit asks when any plan changes, a new recipe only when it would release a reservation; confirm label Save recipe / Save and release. Delete: refused immediately (no dialog) when targeted; otherwise dialog adds the plan consequence (acquire instead / choose another) and release text, label Delete and release when releasing. Tests: planImpact.test.ts (17), RecipeChanges.test.tsx (5).
